arxiv-2107-06735.creator: Ning Ma 1 , Jiajun Bu 1 , Lixian Lu 1 , Jun Wen 2 , Zhen Zhang 1, Sheng Zhou 1 , Xifeng Yan 3
arxiv-2107-06735.description: Abstract . Domain Adaptation has been widely used to deal with the distribution shift in vision, language, multimedia etc. Most domain adaptation methods learn domain-invariant features with data from both domains available. However, such a strategy might be infeasible in practice when source data are unavailable due to data-privacy concerns.

arxiv-2204-00214.title: Toric varieties of Schröder type Thanks: This work was supported by NRF-2020R1A2C1A01011045 and NRF-2021R1A6A1A10044950
arxiv-2204-00214.creator: JiSun Huh, Seonjeong Park
arxiv-2204-00214.description: Abstract . A dissection of a polygon is obtained by drawing diagonals such that no two diagonals intersect in their interiors. In this paper, we define a toric variety of Schröder type as a smooth toric variety associated with a polygon dissection.

arxiv-2204-05305.title: Galaxy and halo angular clustering in Λ ​ CDM \mathrm{\Lambda\text{CDM}} and Modified Gravity cosmologies
arxiv-2204-05305.creator: Paweł Drozda, Wojciech A. Hellwing, Maciej Bilicki
arxiv-2204-05305.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Paweł Drozda, Wojciech A. Hellwing, Maciej Bilicki. Using a suite of N N -body simulations, we study the angular clustering of galaxies, halos, and dark matter in Lambda Cold Dark Matter and modified gravity (MG) scenarios. We consider two general categories of such MG models, one is the f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) gravity, and the other is the normal branch of the Dvali-Gabadadze-Porrati brane world (nDGP).

arxiv-2209-08769.title: Walk-and-Relate: A Random-Walk-based Algorithm for Representation Learning on Sparse Knowledge Graphs
arxiv-2209-08769.creator: Saurav Manchanda
arxiv-2209-08769.description: Abstract . Knowledge graph (KG) embedding techniques use structured relationships between entities to learn low-dimensional representations of entities and relations. The traditional KG embedding techniques (such as TransE and DistMult) estimate these embeddings via simple models developed over observed KG triplets. These approaches differ in their triplet scoring loss functions.

arxiv-2210-11219.title: YOWO-Plus: An Incremental Improvement
arxiv-2210-11219.creator: Jianhua Yang
arxiv-2210-11219.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jianhua Yang. In this technical report, we would like to introduce our updates to YOWO, a real-time method for spatio-temporal action detection. We make a bunch of little design changes to make it better. For network structure, we use the same ones of official implemented YOWO, including 3D-ResNext-101 and YOLOv2, but we use a better pretrained weight of our reimplemented YOLOv2, which is better than the official YOLOv2. We also optimize the label assignment used in YOWO.

arxiv-2303-10855.title: Electron Wave Spin in Excited States
arxiv-2303-10855.creator: Ju Gao and Fang Shen
arxiv-2303-10855.description: Abstract The wave spin of an electron can be fully characterized by the current density calculated from the exact four-spinor solution of the Dirac equation. In the excited states of the electron in a magnetic field-free quantum well, the current density has a multiple vortex topology.

arxiv-2304-01065.title: Towards Reuse and Recycling of Lithium-ion Batteries: Tele-robotics for Disassembly of Electric Vehicle Batteries
arxiv-2304-01065.creator: Jamie Hathaway 1,2,† , Abdelaziz Shaarawy 1,† , Cansu Akdeniz 1 , Ali Aflakian 1,2 , Rustam Stolkin 1,2 , Alireza Rastegarpanah 1,2,∗,
arxiv-2304-01065.description: Abstract Disassembly of electric vehicle batteries is a critical stage in recovery, recycling and re-use of high-value battery materials, but is complicated by limited standardisation, design complexity, compounded by uncertainty and safety issues from varying end-of-life condition. Telerobotics presents an avenue for semi-autonomous robotic disassembly that addresses these challenges.

arxiv-2305-12172.title: Leveraging on-shell interference to search for FCNCs of the top quark and the Z boson
arxiv-2305-12172.creator: Lucas Cremer, Johannes Erdmann, Roni Harnik, Jan Lukas Späh, Emmanuel Stamou
arxiv-2305-12172.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lucas Cremer, Johannes Erdmann, Roni Harnik, Jan Lukas Späh, Emmanuel Stamou. Flavour-changing-neutral currents (FCNCs) involving the top quark are highly suppressed within the Standard Model (SM). Hence, any signal in current or planned future collider experiments would constitute a clear manifestation of physics beyond the SM. We propose a novel, interference-based strategy to search for top-quark FCNCs involving the Z Z boson that has the potential to complement traditional search strategies due to a more favourable luminosity scaling.

arxiv-2306-06642.title: Well-Calibrated Probabilistic Predictive Maintenance using Venn-Abers Thanks: The authors acknowledge the Swedish Knowledge Foundation, Jönköping University, and the industrial partners for financially supporting the research through the AFAIR project with grant number 20200223, as part of the resea
arxiv-2306-06642.creator: Ulf Johansson, Tuwe Löfström, Cecilia Sönströd
arxiv-2306-06642.description: Abstract When using machine learning for fault detection, a common problem is the fact that most data sets are very unbalanced, with the minority class (a fault) being the interesting one. In this paper, we investigate the usage of Venn-Abers predictors, looking specifically at the effect on the minority class predictions.

arxiv-2408-14693.title: Long Range Energy-energy Correlator at the LHC
arxiv-2408-14693.creator: Yuxun Guo, Xiaohui Liu, Feng Yuan
arxiv-2408-14693.description: Abstract We study the forward-backward azimuthal angular correlations of hadrons in association with multi-particle production in the central rapidity region in proton-proton collisions at the LHC. We apply the nucleon energy-energy correlator framework, where the spinning gluon distribution introduces a nontrivial cos ⁡ ( 2 ​ ϕ ) \cos(2\phi) asymmetries.

arxiv-2412-14407.title: Search for an Anomalous Production of Charged-Current ν e \nu_{e} Interactions Without Visible Pions Across Multiple Kinematic Observables in MicroBooNE
arxiv-2412-14407.creator: P. Abratenko, D. Andrade Aldana, L. Arellano, J. Asaadi, A. Ashkenazi, S. Balasubramanian, B. Baller, A. Barnard, G. Barr, D. Barrow, J. Barrow, V. Basque, J. Bateman, O. Benevides Rodrigues, S. Berkman, A. Bhat, M. Bhattacharya, M. Bishai, A. Blake, B. Bogart, T. Bolton, M. B. Brunetti, L. Camiller
arxiv-2412-14407.description: Abstract This Letter presents an investigation of low-energy electron-neutrino interactions in the Fermilab Booster Neutrino Beam by the MicroBooNE experiment, motivated by the excess of electron-neutrino-like events observed by the MiniBooNE experiment. This is the first measurement to use data from all five years of operation of the MicroBooNE experiment, corresponding to an exposure of 1.11 × 10 21 1.

arxiv-2501-12440.title: Pulse and Polarization Structures in Axion-Converted X-rays from Pulsars
arxiv-2501-12440.creator: JiJi Fan, Lingfeng Li, Chen Sun
arxiv-2501-12440.description: Abstract Neutron stars (NS’s) with their strong magnetic fields and hot dense cores could be powerful probes of axions, a classic benchmark of feebly-coupled new particles, through abundant production of axions with the axion-nucleon coupling and subsequent conversion into X-rays due to the axion-photon coupling.

arxiv-2509-00164.title: The potential applications of muography to revealing sea shipwrecks
arxiv-2509-00164.creator: Anzori Sh. Georgadze
arxiv-2509-00164.description: Abstract Muon imaging, a non-invasive technique leveraging naturally occurring cosmic muons, has emerged as a promising tool for exploring underwater objects, including shipwrecks. This article examines the potential of muon imaging to investigate the contents of wrecked ships in the Baltic Sea and other marine environments.

arxiv-2509-05242.title: The anabelian restricted Burnside problem
arxiv-2509-05242.creator: Andreas Thom
arxiv-2509-05242.description: Abstract . Let n , d ∈ ℕ n,d\in\mathbb{N} and w ∈ 𝔽 n w\in\mathbb{F}_{n} be non-trivial. We prove that the relatively free group of rank d d in the variety defined by the group law w w has a largest anabelian finite quotient and estimate its size.

arxiv-2509-20207.title: PU-Gaussian: Point Cloud Upsampling using 3D Gaussian Representation
arxiv-2509-20207.creator: Mahmoud Khater, Mona Strauss, Philipp von Olshausen, Alexander Reiterer
arxiv-2509-20207.description: Abstract Point clouds produced by 3D sensors are often sparse and noisy, posing challenges for tasks requiring dense and high-fidelity 3D representations. Prior work has explored both implicit feature-based upsampling and distance-function learning to address this, but often at the expense of geometric interpretability or robustness to input sparsity.

arxiv-2512-13043.title: GTR-Turbo: Merged Checkpoint is Secretly a Free Teacher for Agentic VLM Training
arxiv-2512-13043.creator: Tong Wei, Yijun Yang, Changhao Zhang, Junliang Xing, Yuanchun Shi, Zongqing Lu, Deheng Ye
arxiv-2512-13043.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tong Wei, Yijun Yang, Changhao Zhang, Junliang Xing, Yuanchun Shi, Zongqing Lu, Deheng Ye. Multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) for multi-modal agents built upon vision–language models (VLMs) is hampered by sparse rewards and long-horizon credit assignment. Recent methods densify the reward by querying a teacher that provides step-level feedback, e.g., Guided Thought Reinforcement (GTR) ( 50 ) and On-Policy Distillation ( 24 ) , but rely on costly, often privileged models as the teacher, limiting practicality and reproducibility.

arxiv-2512-16369.title: A first look at common RPKI publication practices
arxiv-2512-16369.creator: Moritz Müller-Brus, Lisa Bruder, Caspar Schutijser, Ralph Koning
arxiv-2512-16369.description: Abstract . The RPKI ( RPKI ) is crucial for securing the routing system of the Internet. With the RPKI , owners of Internet resources can make cryptographically backed claims, for example about the legitimate origin of their IP space. Thousands of networks use this information to detect malicious or accidental route hijacks.

arxiv-2602-19184.title: Human-to-Robot Interaction: Learning from Video Demonstration for Robot Imitation
arxiv-2602-19184.creator: Thanh Nguyen Canh, Thanh-Tuan Tran, Haolan Zhang, Ziyan Gao, Nak Young Chong, Xiem HoangVan
arxiv-2602-19184.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Thanh Nguyen Canh, Thanh-Tuan Tran, Haolan Zhang, Ziyan Gao, Nak Young Chong, Xiem HoangVan. Learning from Demonstration (LfD) offers a promising paradigm for robot skill acquisition. Recent approaches attempt to extract manipulation commands directly from video demonstrations, yet face two critical challenges: (1) general video captioning models prioritize global scene features over task-relevant objects, producing descriptions unsuitable for precise robotic execution, and (2) end-to-end architectures coupling visual understanding with policy learning require extensive paired datasets and struggle to generalize across objects and scenarios.

arxiv-2604-13988.creator: Mohammad Ahangarkiasari, Andreas Tind Damgaard, Casper Haurum, Kaare B. Mikkelsen

doe-osti-3387219-trip-report-for-foreign.creator: Darby, Flynn Bernard

This trip report summarizes the activities of a NCSP sponsored trip to the 33rd International Meeting on Reactor Noise (IMORN-33) held at the Laboratory of Subatomic Physics & Cosmology (LPSC) in Grenoble, France the week of July 6th, 2026.

pmc-10740059.title: Effect of Urtica dioica L. Essential oil (forms of free and nanoliposome) on some inoculated pathogens (Escherichia coli and Listeria monocytogenes) in minced camel meat
pmc-10740059.creator: Masoudeh Shabani, Azade Ghorbani-HasanSaraei, Nabi Shariatifar, Faezeh Savadkoohi, Seyed-Ahmad Shahidi
pmc-10740059.description: Highlights•The effect of nettle EO on some characteristics of camel meat was investigated.•Nettle essential oil was prepared in two forms, free and nanoliposome.•Various physical, chemical, microbial and sensory tests were measured.•Two inoculated pathogenic bacteria were used to perform microbial tests.•The best preservative effect was related to the nanoliposome form of the EO.

pmc-11331605.title: Factors associated with the non-retention of health sector employees recruited in Iran: a survival analysis
pmc-11331605.creator: Behrooz Rahimi, Faeze Ghasemi Seproo, Roghayeh Khalilnezhad, Mahmoud Khodadost, Tahereh Kashkalani, Fatemeh Younesi, Behzad Tadayon, Mahmood Samadpour, Mahboubeh Bayat
pmc-11331605.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundHealth staff are an essential component of the health system and a significant factor in improving health outcomes. As a result, without a suitable number of trained and supported workforces, health-related goals will not be achieved. As a result, one of the most significant tasks of the government and healthcare human resource management in healthcare organizations is focusing on development and maintenance of personnel.MethodThis study was a longitudinal and historical cohort study.

pmc-11355931.title: Two Decades of CABG in the UK: A Propensity Matched Analysis of Outcomes by Conduit Choice
pmc-11355931.creator: Georgia R. Layton, Shubhra Sinha, Massimo Caputo, Gianni D. Angelini, Daniel P. Fudulu, Mustafa Zakkar
pmc-11355931.description: Background/Objectives: Grafting of LIMA to LAD has long been considered the gold-standard conduit choice for patients undergoing CABG. Despite this, the LSV remains the most used conduit by volume and some patients may not receive even a single arterial conduit. However, the outcomes in this group are not frequently explored.

pmc-11417172.title: STARDUST: A pipeline for the unbiased analysis of astrocyte regional calcium dynamics
pmc-11417172.creator: Yifan Wu, Yanchao Dai, Katheryn B Lefton, Timothy E Holy, Thomas Papouin
pmc-11417172.description: SummaryCalcium imaging has become a popular way to probe astrocyte activity, but few techniques holistically capture discrete calcium signals occurring across the astrocyte domain. Here, we introduce STARDUST, a pipeline for the spatio-temporal analysis of regional dynamics and unbiased sorting of transients from fluorescence recordings of astrocytes.

pmc-12470789.title: Functional Response, Interference, and Predation Efficiency of Diomus guilavoguii (Coleoptera: Coccinellidae) on Paracoccus marginatus (Hemiptera: Pseudococcidae)
pmc-12470789.creator: Qijing Lin, Guoguo Ruan, Mingjie Tang, Xuanjie Guo, Meixiaoyun Yang, Xingmin Wang, Xiaosheng Chen, Valerio Mazzoni, Hong Pang
pmc-12470789.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryParacoccus marginatus is a polyphagous pest that threatens more than 200 plant species. Currently, the most widely applied biological control methods predominantly utilize parasitoid natural enemies, while the application of predatory natural enemies remains relatively limited. This study investigates the predatory behavior of Diomus guilavoguii against Paracoccus marginatus by observing functional responses, search effects and interspecific interference effects under controlled laboratory conditions.

pmc-12592593.title: Sulforaphane: a natural organosulfur having potential to modulate apoptosis and survival signalling in cancer
pmc-12592593.creator: Hemant Joshi, Isha Rani, Vikas Sharma, Ujjawal Sharma, Tanisha Dimri, Manoj Kumar, Ritu Chauhan, Abhishek Chauhan, Damandeep Kaur, Shafiul Haque, Faraz Ahmad, Hardeep Singh Tuli
pmc-12592593.description: Owing to its ever-growing range of pharmacological advantages, sulforaphane, an isothiocyanate from cruciferous vegetables such as broccoli, is becoming increasingly popular. This review aims to provide a thorough understanding and a current update on the application of sulforaphane in cancer treatment.

pmc-12667417.title: The Prevalence of Asymptomatic Bacteriuria Among Jordanian Pregnant Women
pmc-12667417.creator: Ayman Qatawneh, Raghad Abd Elnasser Shaqour, Ibrahim Al-Amayreh, Hisham Abuhussein, Albara’ Abd Alnabi, Motasem Alaiwah, Ala Salim Khatatneh, Abdulrahman Alqatawneh, Fida Thekrallah
pmc-12667417.description: ObjectiveAsymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB) is common in pregnant women and can lead to serious complications. During pregnancy, routine screening for bacteriuria is often not standard in many developing countries, leading to underdiagnosis. In Jordan, there is limited data on ASB in pregnant women. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, causative organisms, antibiotic sensitivity, and associations with maternal conditions and diseases.

pmc-12686777.title: Designing effective clinical education spaces: A scoping review
pmc-12686777.creator: Megan Phelps, Pippa Yeoman, Lynn V Monrouxe
pmc-12686777.description: IntroductionClinical education in health facilities is critical for health professional student learning. However, consideration of health professional students' learning when designing and building hospitals appears to be neglected. Evidence‐based health facility design may encourage student learning and add value to the investment in facilities.

pmc-13074753.title: Natural Alkaloids as Antimicrobial Agents: Mechanisms, Potentials and Challenges
pmc-13074753.creator: Xi-Zhong Zhang, Ming-Xia Chen, Rui Hou, Wan-Qin Wang, Zhen-Dan He, Jie-Shu You, Xun Song
pmc-13074753.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a significant global health threat, with multidrug-resistant pathogens undermining the effectiveness of conventional antibiotics. Natural alkaloids, a diverse group of nitrogen-containing compounds mainly derived from plants, are gaining attention as potential antimicrobial agents due to their broad-spectrum activity, structural variety, and unique mechanisms of action.

pmc-13084109.title: Immunotherapy challenges surgical dogma in placental site trophoblastic tumor
pmc-13084109.creator: J Michael Straughn, Teresa KL Boitano
pmc-13084109.description: standard of care for stage I disease even in young patients for whom fertility loss carries significant consequences. The recent report by Bolze and colleagues challenges that paradigm. A 26-year-old patient with stage I PSTT seeking fertility preservation achieved rapid biochemical remission and radiologic complete response after a single 200 mg dose of the immunotherapy, pembrolizumab.

pmc-13180573.title: Conditional trust pathways in live-streaming commerce: how consumer motivation influences responses to human and AI anchors
pmc-13180573.creator: Yujia Lin, Yue Zou, Xin Wang
pmc-13180573.description: BackgroundAI anchors are increasingly deployed in live-streaming commerce, raising the question of whether they can substitute for human anchors. Prior studies have documented differences in consumer responses to these anchor types, but the psychological processes underlying trust formation remain unclear. This study approaches the question from a media psychology and human-machine communication perspective rather than focusing solely on commercial outcomes.

pmc-13196945.title: Restrictive versus liberal oxygenation targets in patients with acute heart failure and pulmonary congestion–A protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial (The REDOX-AHF trial)
pmc-13196945.creator: Ida Arentz Taraldsen, Anne Sophie Overgaard Olesen, Jasmin Dam Lukoschewitz, Ejvind Frausing Hansen, Olav Wendelboe Nielsen, Christian Hassager, Jens Jakob Thune, Maryam Noory, Arzu Karamat, Jens Dahlgaard Hove, Johannes Grand
pmc-13196945.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionAcute heart failure (AHF) is the cause of one in twenty hospital admissions. Supplemental oxygen therapy is a routine treatment in the management of patients with dyspnea, including those with AHF. Current guidelines recommend oxygen therapy as part of the initial treatment, if peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) is < 90% or partial pressure of arterial oxygen (PaO2) is < 60 mmHg to correct hypoxemia. There is no clear evidence favoring restrictive or liberal oxygenation strategies in patients with acute heart failure.

pmc-13300377.title: Evolutionary Tree for All Bumblebee Species World-Wide Estimated by Combining Information from Fast-Evolving Genes, Slow-Evolving Genes, and Genomic Data (Apidae, Bombus)
pmc-13300377.creator: Paul H. Williams, Pedro Alonso-Alonso, Marina Arbetman, Elaine Françoso, Guillaume Ghisbain, Jiaxing Huang, Michael C. Orr, Zong-Xin Ren, Martin Streinzer, Chawatat Thanoosing, Rémy Vandame, Madeleine Waite, Selina Brace
pmc-13300377.description: Simple SummaryTo estimate the evolutionary tree for all of the world’s bumblebee species, we combine (1) earlier data for mostly slow-evolving nuclear genes, with (2) new data for a fast-evolving mitochondrial gene, and (3) results from a study of genomic data. The resulting tree provides an up-to-date starting point for comparative studies of all bumblebees. 1.

pmc-13318383.title: Bilateral Prostate Artery Embolization for Massive Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia in a Frail Elderly Patient With Recurrent Urinary Retention
pmc-13318383.creator: Ana B Cuni Hernandez, Paige Carruthers, Elizabeth Blanco Espinosa, Idania Cruzata Matos, Claudia A Garcia Gonzalez, Laura Diaz Perez, Raysa Garces Ruiz
pmc-13318383.description: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a highly prevalent condition among elderly men and a major cause of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), urinary retention, recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs), hematuria, and bladder outlet obstruction (BOO). Management of severe BPH in elderly patients with multiple comorbidities remains challenging, particularly in those who are poor surgical candidates.

pmc-13560715.title: Complete genome sequence of Clostridium beijerinckii DSM 105335 obtained by hybrid Illumina- and Nanopore-based assembly
pmc-13560715.creator: Jessica M. O'Loughlin, Emma Allen-Vercoe, Catherine McNay, Sarah Windsor, Louise Horsfall, Karl Burgess
pmc-13560715.description: Clostridium beijerinckii DSM 105335 was originally isolated from wild boar feces in Canada. Here, we report a complete 5,792,971 bp genome sequence for this strain. It was assembled using a hybrid approach utilizing short Illumina paired-end reads and long reads sequenced with an Oxford Nanopore MinION. ANNOUNCEMENT Clostridium spp.

pmc-13580142.title: Bio-Polymers Based Functionalized Hydrogel Carriers for Targeted Oncology Therapies: Current Progress and Future Perspectives
pmc-13580142.creator: Shengchun Qiu, Xiaoyan Wen
pmc-13580142.description: Challenges in cancer therapy remain in terms of lack of tumor selectivity, unwanted side effects, and inefficacy of current treatment strategies. Over the past few years, functionalized bio-polymer gels have become attractive alternatives for cancer therapy, as they are biocompatible and can be tailored to provide local drug delivery.
